label: Real Analysis
shortDescription: Rigorous foundations of calculus. Sequences, continuity, differentiation, integration, and metric spaces.
modulesDescription: Read the real-analysis chapters in order, or jump directly to the topic you need.
ogTitle: Learn Real Analysis for Free | CalcPath
ogDescription: Master rigorous real analysis: the real number system, sequences and series, limits and continuity with ε-δ definitions, differentiation and integration theorems, Lebesgue theory, metric spaces, and advanced topics — with ELI5 explanations, detailed worked examples, and targeted practice questions.
courseDescription: A complete introduction to real analysis providing the rigorous foundations of calculus. Covers construction and properties of real numbers, sequences and convergence, limits and continuity, the derivative and mean value theorems, Riemann and Lebesgue integration, metric spaces and compactness, plus advanced topics like functions of bounded variation and Fourier series. Each lesson includes intuitive ELI5 breakdowns, detailed worked examples, common pitfalls, and targeted practice questions.

topics.title: The Real Number System
topics.description: The reals as a complete ordered field; why Q fails completeness and the same algebra produces sqrt(2) once a supremum exists; the Archimedean property proved from completeness; density of the rationals and irrationals; both the Cauchy and Dedekind constructions with the uniqueness theorem that makes them interchangeable; and Cantor's diagonal argument with the cardinality of the continuum.

topics.title: Sequences & Series
topics.description: Limits of sequences by epsilon-N, the algebra of limits, squeeze and the standard limits; monotone convergence and Bolzano-Weierstrass; the Cauchy criterion and its relation to completeness; series, the harmonic divergence, and the full battery of convergence tests; absolute against conditional convergence with Riemann's rearrangement theorem; and power series with Cauchy-Hadamard and term-by-term operations.

topics.title: Limits & Continuity
topics.description: Limits of functions by epsilon-delta with the laws derived rather than quoted; the sequential characterisation of limits and continuity; the classification of discontinuities; uniform continuity, Lipschitz and Heine-Cantor; the Intermediate Value Theorem proved from completeness; and the Extreme Value Theorem with compactness, each hypothesis shown necessary by counterexample.

topics.title: Differentiation
topics.description: The derivative from the difference quotient; differentiability implies continuity; the differentiation rules proved from the definition, with the chain rule via Caratheodory's formulation; Rolle, the Mean Value Theorem and monotonicity; Cauchy's MVT and L'Hopital's rule; Taylor's theorem with Lagrange, integral, Cauchy and Peano remainders; and the standard counterexamples of a discontinuous derivative and a smooth non-analytic function.

topics.title: Riemann Integration
topics.description: Darboux upper and lower sums, refinement and Riemann's criterion; continuity and monotonicity as sufficient conditions; Lebesgue's criterion stated and located; both parts of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus; improper integrals with the p-tests, comparison and principal value; and Riemann-Stieltjes integrals with integration by parts, unifying sums and integrals.

topics.title: Lebesgue Integration
topics.description: Why the Riemann integral fails under pointwise limits; outer measure, Caratheodory measurability and measurable functions; the integral built from simple functions; the Monotone Convergence Theorem, Fatou's lemma proved from it and Dominated Convergence proved from Fatou; agreement with the Riemann integral; differentiation under the integral sign; and the counterexamples showing domination is necessary.

topics.title: Metric Spaces & Topology
topics.description: Metrics, balls and the topology they generate; open and closed sets, closure, interior and boundary; compactness by open covers, Heine-Borel in R^n, and its equivalence with sequential compactness; completeness, Banach spaces and the completion construction; connectedness and path-connectedness with the topologist's sine curve; the Banach fixed point theorem with convergence rates and Picard-Lindelof; and the Baire category theorem with its generic consequences.

topics.title: Advanced Topics
topics.description: Functions of bounded variation and the Jordan decomposition; absolute continuity, the Cantor function, and the link to the integral; the Lebesgue differentiation theorem via the Hardy-Littlewood maximal function; L^p spaces with Young, Holder, Minkowski and Riesz-Fischer completeness; Fourier series with orthogonality, Bessel, Parseval, Fejer and the Gibbs phenomenon; and rigorous multivariable calculus through Fubini-Tonelli, change of variables and Stokes.
